newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy rail chief arrested in corruption probe.
newsitem.headline: Italy rail chief arrested in corruption probe.

text.p: The managing director of Italy's state railway system has been arrested in a corruption probe into company finances, a magistrate said on Monday.
Lorenzo Necci, 55, was being held in a jail in the northwest coastal town of La Spezia where the investigation was based.

Investigating magistrate Alberto Cardino told reporters in La Spezia that Necci, arrested on Sunday at his country home near Rome, was detained on suspicion of criminal association, fraud, embezzlement, abuse of office, false accounting and corruption.
Necci has been overseeing a plan to launch a multi-billion dollar high-speed railway which, when it gets off the ground, is expected to be one of Europe's biggest construction projects.
Cardino would only say that the probe dealt with the finances of the railway system, Ferrovie dello Stato. He said magistrates would interview Necci on Wednesday.
Defence attorney Federico Stella confirmed that Necci had been arrested, but said he had not been briefed by magistrates about the specifics of the case.
The news agency ANSA, quoting judicial sources, said the magistrates were probing suspected embezzlement of funds from the railroad and its subsidiaries.
Two businessmen and a secretary had also been arrested on similar charges, media reported.
Trade union leaders who worked closely with Necci said they were worried about how Necci's arrest would affect the high-speed project.
"A vacuum in leadership at this phase could be fatal to the soundness of the company," said Walter Cerfeda, a top official of the CGIL trades union grouping.
"I'm shocked," said Paolo Brutti, secretary general of the FILT-CIGL union representing railway workers.
"For the unions, Necci's arrest was a surprise, but also the source of great worry for the launch of major works on the railway infrastructure and the modernisation of the system."
Labour Minister Tiziano Treu, asked at a convention in southern Italy to comment on Necci's arrest, said: "The major projects (of the railroad) must continue".
